justice: Total absence of sidewalks restricts accessibility for wheelchair users and the elderly, failing barrier-free design needs.
Allocation of the entire right-of-way to wide motor vehicle lanes shows extremely poor equity, marginalizing active transport users.
Complete lack of tactile paving and safe pedestrian crossing facilities makes the environment unfair and hazardous for visually impaired individuals.
safety: High-speed multi-lane design without physical separation for vulnerable road users creates severe safety risks for any pedestrians or cyclists.
Distance check markings on the road surface and the green '50m' sign improve following distance safety and awareness for drivers.
Continuous metal guardrails on both sides protect vehicles from running off the road but trap any pedestrians who might be present, reducing escape options.
livability: Absence of ground-floor destinations, shops, or community facilities results in zero street vitality and fails to meet daily needs.
The environment functions purely as a high-speed transit corridor with no social spaces or resting places for teenagers or older adults to interact.
Prominent high-voltage power lines and transmission towers in the background detract from the neighborhood's livability and residential quality.
sustainability: Lack of public transit stops or dedicated bus lanes encourages heavy reliance on private, carbon-emitting motor vehicles.
Absence of bicycle infrastructure completely discourages zero-emission active travel options.
Extensive impermeable asphalt surface limits natural rainwater infiltration, though the roadside green buffers offer minimal ecological support.
aesthetics: The visual landscape is heavily dominated by grey asphalt and intrusive high-voltage power lines, reducing scenic appeal.
Well-maintained roadside hedges and manicured green buffers provide a neat but visually monotonous edge.
Lack of human-scale street furniture or varied architectural elements makes the environment visually uninviting for all social groups.
comfort: Complete lack of benches or resting facilities makes the area highly uncomfortable and unusable for elderly pedestrians.
Absence of canopy shade trees over the paved area exposes any potential active users to extreme thermal discomfort in hot weather.
The open high-speed traffic environment generates significant noise and psychological stress for any non-motorized users.
walkability: Complete absence of paved sidewalks makes pedestrian movement physically impossible and fundamentally unsafe.
Continuous metal guardrails act as physical barriers, preventing any pedestrian permeability or lateral movement.
Lack of pedestrian crosswalks, overpasses, or signals severs any potential walking routes across the highway corridor.
bikeability: No dedicated or protected bike lanes exist, forcing any cyclists to mix with dangerous high-speed motor traffic.
Lack of bicycle parking, wayfinding signage, or safe intersection designs indicates an environment completely hostile to cycling.
High vehicle speeds and multi-lane designs maximize conflict risks, entirely deterring cycling for vulnerable groups like adolescents and the elderly.
